questions.prompt: The polynomial $f(x)=x^3-7x^2+14x-8$. (a) Show that $x=2$ is a root. (2) (b) Factorise $f(x)$ completely. (3) (c) Hence solve $f(x)=0$. (1)
questions.solution: (a) Substituting $x=2$ gives zero. (b) The roots are $1,2,4$, so $f(x)=(x-1)(x-2)(x-4)$. (c) $x=1,2,4$. [M1 A1 B1 M1 A1 B1]

questions.prompt: The line $L$ has equation $y=2x+4$. (a) State its gradient. (1) (b) Find the equation of the line perpendicular to $L$ through $(2,3)$. (3) (c) Find the $x$-coordinate where this perpendicular meets the $x$-axis. (2)
questions.solution: (a) Gradient $2$. (b) Perpendicular gradient $=-0.5$, so $y-3=-0.5(x-2)$, equivalently $y=-0.5x+4.0$. (c) Set $y=0$: $x=8.0$. [M1 A1 B1 M1 A1 B1]

questions.prompt: A geometric sequence has first term 3 and common ratio 1.2. (a) Find the 8th term. (2) (b) Find the sum of the first 8 terms. (3) (c) Explain why the sequence has no finite sum to infinity. (1)
questions.solution: (a) $u_8=3(1.2)^7=10.750$. (b) $S_8=3((1.2)^8-1)/(1.2-1)=49.497$. (c) Since $|r|>1$, the terms do not tend to zero and the infinite sum diverges. [M1 A1 B1 M1 A1 B1]

questions.prompt: A geometric sequence has first term 3 and common ratio 1.2. (a) Find the 8th term. (2) (b) Find the sum of the first 8 terms. (3) (c) Explain why the sequence has no finite sum to infinity. (1)
questions.solution: (a) $u_8=3(1.2)^7=10.750$. (b) $S_8=3((1.2)^8-1)/(1.2-1)=49.497$. (c) Since $|r|>1$, the terms do not tend to zero and the infinite sum diverges. [M1 A1 B1 M1 A1 B1]

questions.solution: (a) $\frac{dy}{dx}=e^{-4x}(3x^{2}-4x^3)=x^{2}e^{-4x}(3-4x)$. (b) Positive stationary point at $x=3/4=0.750$. (c) Show the derivative changes from positive to negative or evaluate the second derivative and show it is negative. [M1 A1 B1 M1 A1 B1 M1]

questions.prompt: Solve $x^2-5x+6=0$ and explain how the discriminant determines the number of real roots of a quadratic equation. (5)
questions.solution: $x^2-5x+6=(x-2)(x-3)$, so $x=2$ or $3$. For $ax^2+bx+c=0$, discriminant $b^2-4ac$: positive gives two distinct real roots, zero gives one repeated real root, negative gives no real roots. [M1 A1 B1 M1 A1]

questions.solution: $x^2-5x+6=(x-2)(x-3)$, so $x=2$ or $3$. For $ax^2+bx+c=0$, discriminant $b^2-4ac$: positive gives two distinct real roots, zero gives one repeated real root, negative gives no real roots. [M1 A1 B1 M1 A1]

questions.solution: $x^2-5x+6=(x-2)(x-3)$, so $x=2$ or $3$. For $ax^2+bx+c=0$, discriminant $b^2-4ac$: positive gives two distinct real roots, zero gives one repeated real root, negative gives no real roots. [M1 A1 B1 M1 A1]

questions.prompt: $\mathbf a=(3,2,1)$. (a) Find $|\mathbf a|$. (2) (b) Find a unit vector in the direction of $\mathbf a$. (2) (c) Explain what it means for two vectors to be perpendicular in terms of their scalar product. (1)
hints: Magnitude is the square root of the sum of squared components.
questions.solution: (a) $|\mathbf a|=\sqrt{14}=3.742$. (b) Unit vector $=\frac1{3.742}(3,2,1)$. (c) Their scalar product is zero. [M1 A1 B1 M1 A1]

questions.prompt: $X\sim B(20,0.2)$. (a) Find $E(X)$ and $\mathrm{Var}(X)$. (2) (b) Write down $P(X=0)$ exactly in terms of powers and calculate it. (2) (c) State two conditions for a binomial model. (2)
hints: For a binomial variable use $np$ and $np(1-p)$.
questions.solution: (a) $E(X)=np=4.0$ and variance $=np(1-p)=3.2$. (b) $P(X=0)=(0.8)^{20}=0.01153$. (c) Fixed number of independent trials, two outcomes per trial and constant success probability. [M1 A1 B1 M1 A1 B1]

questions.prompt: $X\sim B(30,0.3)$. (a) Find $E(X)$ and $\mathrm{Var}(X)$. (2) (b) Write down $P(X=0)$ exactly in terms of powers and calculate it. (2) (c) State two conditions for a binomial model. (2)
hints: For a binomial variable use $np$ and $np(1-p)$.
questions.solution: (a) $E(X)=np=9.0$ and variance $=np(1-p)=6.3$. (b) $P(X=0)=(0.7)^{30}=0.00002$. (c) Fixed number of independent trials, two outcomes per trial and constant success probability. [M1 A1 B1 M1 A1 B1]

questions.prompt: $X\sim B(20,0.2)$. (a) Find $E(X)$ and $\mathrm{Var}(X)$. (2) (b) Write down $P(X=0)$ exactly in terms of powers and calculate it. (2) (c) State two conditions for a binomial model. (2)
hints: For a binomial variable use $np$ and $np(1-p)$.

questions.prompt: A particle moves in a straight line with initial speed 4 m s$^{-1}$ and constant acceleration 1.5 m s$^{-2}$. (a) Find its speed after 5 s. (2) (b) Find the distance travelled in this time. (3) (c) State one modelling assumption in treating the particle as a point mass. (1)
questions.solution: (a) $v=u+at=4+1.5(5)=11.5$ m s$^{-1}$. (b) $s=ut+\frac12at^2=38.75$ m. (c) Its dimensions/rotation are neglected relative to the motion being modelled. [M1 A1 B1 M1 A1 B1]

questions.prompt: A particle moves in a straight line with initial speed 6 m s$^{-1}$ and constant acceleration 2 m s$^{-2}$. (a) Find its speed after 5 s. (2) (b) Find the distance travelled in this time. (3) (c) State one modelling assumption in treating the particle as a point mass. (1)
questions.solution: (a) $v=u+at=6+2(5)=16$ m s$^{-1}$. (b) $s=ut+\frac12at^2=55.0$ m. (c) Its dimensions/rotation are neglected relative to the motion being modelled. [M1 A1 B1 M1 A1 B1]

questions.prompt: A particle moves in a straight line with initial speed 6 m s$^{-1}$ and constant acceleration 2 m s$^{-2}$. (a) Find its speed after 5 s. (2) (b) Find the distance travelled in this time. (3) (c) State one modelling assumption in treating the particle as a point mass. (1)
questions.solution: (a) $v=u+at=6+2(5)=16$ m s$^{-1}$. (b) $s=ut+\frac12at^2=55.0$ m. (c) Its dimensions/rotation are neglected relative to the motion being modelled. [M1 A1 B1 M1 A1 B1]

questions.prompt: A particle moves in a straight line with initial speed 8 m s$^{-1}$ and constant acceleration 2.5 m s$^{-2}$. (a) Find its speed after 5 s. (2) (b) Find the distance travelled in this time. (3) (c) State one modelling assumption in treating the particle as a point mass. (1)
questions.solution: (a) $v=u+at=8+2.5(5)=20.5$ m s$^{-1}$. (b) $s=ut+\frac12at^2=71.25$ m. (c) Its dimensions/rotation are neglected relative to the motion being modelled. [M1 A1 B1 M1 A1 B1]

questions.prompt: Solve $x^2-5x+6=0$ and explain how the discriminant determines the number of real roots of a quadratic equation. (5)
questions.solution: $x^2-5x+6=(x-2)(x-3)$, so $x=2$ or $3$. For $ax^2+bx+c=0$, discriminant $b^2-4ac$: positive gives two distinct real roots, zero gives one repeated real root, negative gives no real roots. [M1 A1 B1 M1 A1]

questions.solution: $x^2-5x+6=(x-2)(x-3)$, so $x=2$ or $3$. For $ax^2+bx+c=0$, discriminant $b^2-4ac$: positive gives two distinct real roots, zero gives one repeated real root, negative gives no real roots. [M1 A1 B1 M1 A1]
